globalRequirements: Audit the exact VELA foundation/application source against the promoted engine-neutral technical design and its current G7-G9/application-lifecycle intent; do not treat historical Drive material as execution authority.

The promoted core is engine-neutral: durable checkpoints/canonical state, durable event log and causal lineage, replay planning, replaceable selector, target-free evidence boundary, prepare-validate-commit/rollback transaction, conservative full-replay fallback, previous-engine safety, audit and compare-and-set protection.
The core must not import or embed a final optimized inference backend, PyTorch/rwkv.cpp implementation details, model weights, final hardware assumptions, or a frozen final backbone policy.

RWKV/model-specific logic belongs at the adapter/evidence edge. Target-free current-lineage evidence may influence anchor choice; target/future/W3-native oracle leakage is forbidden and non-target-free evidence must not weaken full-replay safety.
Synthetic G7 evidence and benchmark results must not be generalized into proof of general identity, production latency, production backend quality, or long-duration real-world robustness.
The audit is read-only. Model findings have HYPOTHESIS_ONLY authority, coding reasoner count is zero, automatic paid retry is zero, and no finding may auto-mutate/merge/deploy.

bundles.name: core types, audit records, traces, results and validation contracts
requirements: Core data contracts must preserve engine-neutral semantics and must not smuggle model/backend-specific state into generic identities, traces, or validation outcomes.
Audit/trace/result structures must represent actual transaction/evidence decisions without silently upgrading hypothesis/benchmark evidence into canonical production truth.
Validation outcomes must fail conservatively when required evidence is absent or inconsistent rather than manufacturing a successful state.

bundles.name: durable checkpoint repository, canonical state persistence, retention and G8 I/O behavior
requirements: Checkpoint and canonical-state persistence must preserve durable identity/version semantics and must not expose a partially written state as canonical.
Retention may remove only data that policy permits; it must not destroy state required to recover the current canonical lineage or silently rewrite identity.
G8 durable-I/O benchmarking is evidence collection only; it must not freeze checkpoint interval/policy or mutate production policy as a side effect.

bundles.name: durable event log, lineage reconstruction, trajectory and process recovery
requirements: Durable events must reconstruct causal lineage deterministically across a fresh process and must not create impossible parent/child history.
Recovery may repair/truncate only an incomplete trailing event caused by process death; complete corruption must remain fatal rather than being silently discarded.
Recovered lineage and trajectory must agree with the persisted canonical/checkpoint state used for subsequent replay planning.

bundles.name: semantic replay scope, equivalence, anchor selection and upgrade planning
requirements: Replay planning must preserve live-cause/current-lineage scope and use conservative full replay when anchor/equivalence evidence is insufficient.
Anchor selection must be replaceable and bounded; it must not use future/target oracle information or reinterpret evaluation-only evidence as selection evidence.
Equivalence must be based on the intended functional/current-lineage contract, not merely structural equality that can hide behavior loss.
Upgrade scope/selection must not mutate canonical state before validation/commit.

bundles.name: guarded replay executor, transaction commit/rollback and resilience
requirements: The guarded path must implement prepare -> validate -> canonical commit, with rollback/fallback when validation or target activation cannot safely complete.
Preflight and execution must share one audited selector/evidence decision instead of evaluating an expensive/model-backed selector twice with potentially divergent results.
Canonical state must never expose an invalid target as committed. Failure handling must preserve or recover the previous valid engine/state path.
Transaction/audit identity must remain coherent across anchor selection, prepare, validation, commit, fallback and rollback.

bundles.name: RWKV adapter, target-free evidence provider and audited G7 bridge
requirements: RWKV backend owns model/token/state details while the foundation core consumes an engine-neutral adapter/evidence contract.
Evidence provider must receive the real inner-selector baseline and consider only eligible carried-generation checkpoints no later than that baseline.
Target-free current-lineage signatures are selection evidence; target output, W3-native future oracle, or other non-target-free evidence is forbidden for anchor choice.
The evidence bridge must reproduce audited selector/provenance decisions without claiming to rerun the model or prove production performance.
Model-specific evidence may make a conservative selection more informed but must never weaken the full-replay fallback/safety decision.

bundles.name: upgrade lifecycle journal, application host, activation/compensation and G9 process recovery
requirements: Application lifecycle orchestration must quiesce/flush the current engine, invoke the guarded upgrade, and activate the target only after a valid canonical commit.

On target activation/lifecycle failure the previous engine/state must remain available for compensation/reactivation; recovery must not double-activate an engine already restored by lifecycle recovery.
Lifecycle journal state must survive process death and make incomplete transitions recoverable without inventing a successful transition or duplicating canonical commits.
Host/store identity guards must prevent executing an upgrade through mismatched ownership/state stores.
G9 failure-matrix tooling is validation evidence only and must not mutate final architecture or production policy.

bundles.name: cross-layer promoted foundation invariants
requirements: Cross-layer regression must exercise the promoted engine-neutral foundation invariants rather than hide contract drift behind mocks that no longer match production-facing interfaces.
A passing regression is evidence for the tested scope only; it must not freeze final backbone/schema/selector policy or convert synthetic validation into production certainty.
